# R145 — Exact phase-fiber mass conservation and Sturmian support-width sum rule

Date: 2026-11-14 (Asia/Shanghai). Status: AUTHOR-SIDE EXACT PROOF / NOT_REVIEWED.
Frozen scientific input: \`43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34\`.
Scope: the external scalar tied-phase S23 mechanical-word observer; no native X6 claim.
Prior results used: R136/R137 event counting, R143 exact prefix-pair membership and R143B phase-block multiplicity. Independently derivable event/counting proof is given below. R143 sources:

## 1. Exact object and BRC-style fiber

Fix integers m>=1, K>=2 and L=K-1>=1. For 0<t<1 define
\[
 S_i^{(K)}(t)=\lfloor(L+i+1)t\rfloor-\lfloor(L+i)t\rfloor,\quad 0\le i<m.
\]
Let W_m denote the complete finite Sturmian language of length m; it contains all realized binary words.

For a binary word w and integer N, define its exact phase fiber
\[
 I_{N,w}=\{0<t<1:\lfloor Lt\rfloor=N,\ S^{(K)}(t)=w\}.
\]
Define \(C_w(K)=\#\{N:I_{N,w}\ne\varnothing\}\).
These integers count distinct *floor-phase blocks*, not distinct words and not Lebesgue measure. They retain the phase index N lost by collapsing each fiber to its word.

With prefix sums \(s_0=0,s_j=\sum_{i<j}w_i\), the fiber is exactly
\[
 I_{N,w}=(0,1)\cap\bigcap_{j=0}^m
 [ (N+s_j)/(L+j),\ (N+s_j+1)/(L+j) ).
\]
It is an interval or empty, and if nonempty has a nonempty open interior. Thus one N yields at most one phase block of word w; the original floor observer has no isolated singleton word-only fibers.

## 2. R145.1 — Exact totient-fiber conservation

Let \(\varphi\) be Euler's totient function and set
\[
 t_q(L,m)=\lfloor(L+m)/q\rfloor-\lfloor(L-1)/q\rfloor.
\]
For all m>=1,K>=2:
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{w\in W_m} C_w(K)
 =1+\sum_{q=2}^{L+m}\varphi(q)\,\mathbf1[t_q(L,m)\ge1].}\tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, the same count has the short collision formula
\[
 \boxed{\sum_w C_w(K)
 =(m+1)L+\binom m2-\sum_{q=2}^{m}\varphi(q)\bigl(t_q(L,m)-1\bigr).}\tag{2}
\]
In particular the *exact uniform mass bounds* are
\[
 \boxed{(m+1)L\le\sum_w C_w(K)\le (m+1)L+\binom m2.}\tag{3}
\]
The correction is nonnegative, uniformly bounded in the arbitrarily large coefficient K, and periodic in L with period \(\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,m)\).

**Proof.** The vector
\((\lfloor Lt\rfloor,\ldots,\lfloor(L+m)t\rfloor)\)
determines and is determined by the pair \((N,w)\). Its entries change only at reduced rational points a/q in (0,1) whose denominator divides at least one integer n in [L,L+m]. Between consecutive such points the vector is constant; at every point at least one entry jumps, and right-continuity ensures the point belongs to the next interval. Each pair (N,w) has an interval fiber, so it cannot recur after a change. Therefore the number of distinct nonempty phase blocks equals one plus the number of different rational change points. For every reduced denominator q there are precisely \(\varphi(q)\) such points, present iff \(t_q\ge1\). This proves (1).

Counting all unreduced pairs a/n with n in [L,L+m] and 1<=a<n gives
\(\sum_{n=L}^{L+m}(n-1)=(m+1)(L-1)+m(m+1)/2\).
A reduced point of denominator q is counted \(t_q\) times. For q>m, \(t_q\le1\) because the interval contains only m+1 consecutive integers. For 2<=q<=m one has \(t_q\ge1\); subtract \(\varphi(q)(t_q-1)\) to remove the duplicates, and add the initial interval. Simplification yields (2).

Among m+1 consecutive integers the number of multiples of q satisfies
\(1\le t_q\le1+\lfloor m/q\rfloor\) for q<=m. Euler's identity
\(\sum_{q\mid n}\varphi(q)=n\) gives
\[
\sum_{q=2}^m\varphi(q)\lfloor m/q\rfloor
=\sum_{n=1}^{m}n-m=\binom m2.
\]
Hence the collision sum lies in [0,binom(m,2)], establishing (3). The t_q functions depend only on L mod q, which establishes the claimed periodicity of the bounded correction. QED.

## 3. R145.2 — Exact support-width mass identity

For w in W_m, let \((\alpha_w,\beta_w)\) be the open interval of slopes admitting a freely chosen intercept for w; it is computed exactly from the prefix bounds
\[
\alpha_w=\max\bigl(0,\max_{i<j}(s_j-s_i-1)/(j-i)\bigr),
\quad
\beta_w=\min\bigl(1,\min_{i<j}(s_j-s_i+1)/(j-i)\bigr).
\]
Then, **for every integer m>=1**,
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{w\in W_m}(\beta_w-\alpha_w)=m+1.}\tag{4}
\]

**Proof.** Fix an irrational slope t in (0,1). As an intercept r moves around [0,1), the breakpoints \(-jt\bmod1\), 0<=j<=m, are distinct and yield m+1 nonempty intervals. Any prescribed word w has its intercept region given by the intersection of m+1 intervals
\([s_j-jt,s_j+1-jt)\cap[0,1)\), hence that region is connected. Therefore the m+1 intercept intervals have m+1 different length-m words. Equivalently, for almost every t,
\(\sum_{w\in W_m}\mathbf1[\alpha_w<t<\beta_w]=m+1\).
There are finitely many words, so integrate over t in (0,1) to obtain (4). QED.

## 4. R145.3 — Limiting distribution over *discrete phase blocks*

For fixed m define \(p_K(w)=C_w(K)/\sum_vC_v(K)\). R143B's exact prefix-pair estimate gives
\(C_w(K)=L(\beta_w-\alpha_w)+O_m(1)\).
Together with (2)–(4), for every w in W_m,
\[
 \boxed{\lim_{K\to\infty}p_K(w)
 =\frac{\beta_w-\alpha_w}{m+1}.}\tag{5}
\]
The right-hand side sums to 1 exactly. This is a distribution over *the distinct nonempty phase-index blocks*, NOT a distribution over uniformly chosen t or uniformly chosen words.

For a completely explicit finite-K error bound, reuse R143B's
\(|C_w(K)-L(\beta_w-\alpha_w)|\le E_m=2m(m+1)+3\).
Writing \(B_m=\binom m2\), (3) gives
\[
 \left|p_K(w)-\frac{\beta_w-\alpha_w}{m+1}\right|
 \le\frac{E_m}{(m+1)L}+\frac{B_m}{(m+1)^2L}.\tag{6}
\]
This follows by subtracting fractions with denominator \(S=\sum C\ge(m+1)L\), using \(0\le S-(m+1)L\le B_m\) and \(0<\beta-\alpha\le1\).

## 5. Exact finite regression and an optional next conjecture

The attached \`check_r145.py\` independently enumerates all 2^m candidate words for m=1..10, constructs the exact support interval and prefix-pair integer phase bounds, and checks equations (1), (3), (4). It crosschecks the complete chronological rational phase partition for 98 (m,K) instances, using exact Fraction midpoints. Totals: 458 distinct Sturmian word records, 11,616 word/coefficient pairs, and 98 independent event-partition comparisons. Output: \`R145_EXACT_FIBER_MASS_PASS\`.

A separate exploratory test asks whether the R143 projected interval at \(L=E(m)-1\), with
\(E(m)=(m-2)\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor+1\),
has width >1 for all words other than \(10^{m-2}1\) and its complement. For m=5..10 every nonextremal word passes, with minimum widths recorded in \`verification_r145.json\`. **This remains a conjectural route and is not used in the proof of (1)–(6).** It could establish the unresolved general formula T(m)=E(m) when combined with R139B's sharp extremal-word condition.

The exact phase index N is the retained fiber label analogous to a positive-integer BRC multiplicity carrier. Summing C_w demonstrates exactly what aggregate word-support counts erase; no signed/complex cancellation, independent review, native X6 map or Foundation promotion is asserted.
